— Parking, Move Over, Steer It-Clear It","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Parking, Move Over, Steer It-Clear It

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
You own the duty to leave your parked car where it cannot turn into a road hazard [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Choose a marked parking area when one exists; forced onto the roadway, sit as far from traffic as you can, hugging within 18 inches of any curb [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Settle far enough from every travel lane that passing traffic flows past untouched [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
Scan traffic before swinging a door open, and climb out on the curb side whenever needed [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Heed every posted parking ban or limit plus colored curb paint, since many no-park areas are signed that way [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
Never park on a crosswalk or square in front of any public or private driveway [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
Bridges beyond city limits and highway tunnels are both off-limits for parking [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
Pulling alongside another stopped or parked car to double-park is forbidden [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
Keep at least five feet from a fire hydrant and stay out of any marked hydrant red zone [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A01
Hold at least 10 feet back from a stop sign [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A01
Hold at least 20 feet back from a fire station entrance [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A01
Hold at least 50 feet back from a railroad crossing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A01
Stay out of signed no-parking zones, often flagged by yellow curbs or pavement lines, and never park inside an intersection [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A01
Sidewalks, interstates, and highways all ban parking outright [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A01
A disability-reserved space is legal only with a Persons with Disabilities Parking Permit [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A02
Iowa move-over law orders a lane change past any stopped rig flashing its lights, from emergency, tow, recovery, maintenance, construction, and waste or recycling trucks down to an ordinary car blinking its hazards [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A02
Where shifting lanes is impossible, illegal, or unsafe, slow to a reasonable and proper pace for conditions and stand ready to halt [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A02
Breaking the move-over law can suspend your license for up to one year [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A02
After a crash with nobody hurt, Iowa law makes you steer an operable car that can move safely out of the travel lanes [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A02
Every minute a blocked interstate lane lingers, the chance of a second crash climbs by roughly 2.8 percent [A02].
Why it matters: the rising secondary-crash risk is the reason clearing comes before exchanging details.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0022]

Misconceptions: an unposted curb is not automatically legal parking since colored curbs and signs also ban it; hazard lights on a stopped car trigger the move-over duty just like an emergency rig; clearing drivable cars after a no-injury crash is the law, not a courtesy.

Mnemonic: hydrant five, sign ten, station twenty, rails fifty; see flashers, change lanes or slow; no hurt, move it.

Glossary: double parking (halting alongside another stopped or parked car); move-over law (the duty to change lanes or slow for stopped flashing-light vehicles); steer-it-clear-it (the duty to clear operable cars from lanes after an injury-free crash); hydrant red zone (a marked no-park area at a fire hydrant).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every parking, move-over, and clear-it rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
